name: Chemin de Fer
description: Chemin de Fer is the original version of Baccarat, popularized in French casinos and famously played by James Bond in the original 007 novels. Unlike its modern cousin, Punto Banco, where all moves are mechanical, Chemin de Fer is a social and strategic game where players take turns acting as the Banker and make active drawing decisions. The name, French for 'Railway', refers to how the dealing shoe travels around the table like a train.

The name, French for 'Railway', refers to how the dealing shoe travels around the table like a train.
Emerging in late 19th-century France as a modification of the older Baccarat Banque. It became the preferred game of European high society during the Belle Ã‰poque.
Variable, typically 8 to 12. One player acts as Banker; others are 'Punters'.
Special oval Baccarat table, a 'Sabot' (shoe) for dealing, a 'Palette' for moving cards, and a discard cylinder.
The Banker deals two face-down hands: one for 'The Player' (representing all Punters) and one for 'The Banker'.

items.text: Baccarat Banque: The position of Banker is auctioned off or held longer, and the Banker plays against two separate hands at once.
